_comment:
Diet engine quality baseline, re-recorded 2026-09-18 on the CORRECTED engine. Everything recorded before this date is INVALID and must not be restored.

WHY THE PREVIOUS BASELINE WAS INVALID. `find_recipe` passed the recent DISHES into the augmenting food picker, and `_pick` reads that argument as FOOD ids (`if food.id in recent: weight *= RECENCY_PENALTY`). Two different tables, one number space. Where the ranges overlapped — every freshly created database, both sequences starting at 1 — a food was cut to a tenth of its weight because a RECIPE happened to share its number; where they did not overlap the penalty never applied. So the engine's output depended on primary keys. Proven by shifting only diet_recipe.id by +100000 on one database, leaving every row otherwise identical:
  recipe ids      max repeats/week   dish rate   distinct dishes
  1..105          4                  0.8810      68
  100001..100105  3                  0.8929      65
The old baseline was recorded on a reseeded development database (high ids), so it described one accidental draw of that collision. A fresh install — CI, and production on day one — got the other, which is why two gate tests failed on every clean database while passing on the developer's. The ids are out of the engine now: the same data measures identically at both ranges. Similarity ties are settled by name for the same reason.

WEEKLY SERVING CAP: 3, chosen by the owner on 2026-09-18. `find_recipe` also leaked the cap — when every fitting dish was at its limit it returned its closest match anyway and the caller accepted it, so WEEK_MAX_SERVINGS = 2 still allowed five servings of one dish in a client's week. An over-cap dish is now not offered at all and the slot falls to the template path. Measured on the corrected engine:
  cap   max repeats/week   dish rate   distinct dishes
  2     2                  0.8214      65
  3     3                  0.8512      64
  4     4                  0.8690      64
Three keeps most of the named-dish rate while holding repetition below what reads as a pattern.

WHAT MOVED against the invalid baseline, and why each is honest: dish rate 0.8929 -> 0.8512 and distinct dishes 65 -> 64, because the cap now binds — about seven of 168 meals become a built plate instead of a dish served a fourth time. Preference satisfaction 0.6875 -> 0.6250 and chosen-ingredient share 0.2411 -> 0.2308, because the recency penalty now lands on the foods it was written for: under the collision a client's chosen food escaped the penalty whenever no recipe shared its id, which flattered both numbers. Worst calorie drift and absurd portions are unchanged, and days with a repeated dish stays 0.

EARLIER DELIBERATE TRADES THAT STILL HOLD. The pool's structure score is bounded by STRUCTURE_CEILING so an explicit choice always outranks a merely well-fitting food. The template shortlist is 20 (measured: 12 could not reach chosen staples, 30 was worse on drift and distinct dishes). A substitution may never replace the ingredient a dish is named after. `min_distinct_portions_per_food` is measured over engine-BUILT plates only, because a recipe author's pinned clove of garlic is meant to be identical every time. `_plan_meal`'s ranking still places "inside tolerance" above the serving count, pinned by test_a_fitting_dish_at_the_weekly_cap_beats_a_plate_that_misses: the cap must never hand the client an off-target plate.
